gloss: to form; to shape; to mold

definitions.gloss: to form; to shape; to mold
definitions.explanation: To give shape or structure to something, either physically or abstractly.

examples.japanese: {粘土|ねんど}で{形作|かたちづく}る。
{経験|けいけん}が{人格|じんかく}を{形作|かたちづく}る。
{長|なが}い{歴史|れきし}の{中|なか}で{独自|どくじ}の{文化|ぶんか}が{形作|かたちづく}られてきた。
examples.english: A unique culture has been formed over the course of a long history.

notes:
A compound verb from {形|かたち} (shape, form) and {作|つく}る (to make). It emphasizes the process of bringing something into a definite shape or structure, whether physical objects or abstract concepts like character, society, or culture.

The passive form {形作|かたちづく}られる is very common, especially when describing how something has been shaped by external forces over time.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人格|じんかく}を{形作|かたちづく}る: to shape one's character
- {文化|ぶんか}を{形作|かたちづく}る: to form a culture
- {社会|しゃかい}を{形作|かたちづく}る: to shape society
- {未来|みらい}を{形作|かたちづく}る: to shape the future

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {作|つく}る: to make — more general; focuses on creation rather than giving shape
- {形成|けいせい}する: to form — more formal and often used in written or academic contexts
- {造|つく}る: to build, to construct — emphasizes physical construction
